text: random walk model instead simulates particles moving wind rose. time step, particles move cell neighbors rates set conductances, spread along routes proportion much wind flows along , rather along fastest one. Particles removed air constant rate, set half-life hours, particles removed cell make deposition. random_walk() two modes. "pulse" mode, particles released tracked time, shows release spreads drifts. airborne particles single release one, three, seven days, half-life three days, shown relative peak density (total airborne mass declines particles deposited):  "stream" mode, particles released continuously, model returns long-run steady state: share particles airborne cell (residence), share deposited cell (deposition). suits processes integrate many releases, seed rain gene flow. Like least-cost models, random walks can run either direction. downwind walk shows particles released site end , upwind walk shows particles deposited site came (origin layer): half-life controls far particles travel: short half-lives keep close source, long half-lives let spread across landscape, long-lived propagules gene flow many generations. trans = 1 winds m/s, hours.
code: pulse <- random_walk(rose, site, mode = "pulse", half_life = 72,                      iter = 168, record = c(24, 72, 168))  d <- as.data.frame(pulse$airborne, xy = TRUE) d <- data.frame(d[c("x", "y")], hours = rep(c(24, 72, 168), each = nrow(d)),                 density = unlist(d[-(1:2)])) d$hours <- factor(paste(d$hours, "hours"), levels = paste(c(24, 72, 168), "hours")) d$density <- d$density / ave(d$density, d$hours, FUN = max) # relative to each panel's peak d$density <- pmax(d$density, 1e-3) # cells the particles haven't reached are exactly zero  ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +       geom_raster(aes(fill = density)) +       geom_path(data = states, aes(long, lat, group = group), color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +       annotate("point", site[1], site[2], color = "red", size = 1) +       facet_wrap(~hours) +       scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "relative\ndensity", trans = "log10",                            limits = c(1e-3, 1), oob = scales::squish) +       coord_quickmap(xlim = c(-120, -90), ylim = c(30, 50), expand = FALSE) +       theme_void() +       theme(strip.text = element_text(margin = margin(4, 0, 4, 0))) down <- random_walk(rose, site, mode = "stream", direction = "downwind", half_life = 48) up <- random_walk(rose, site, mode = "stream", direction = "upwind", half_life = 48)

text: named vector summary statistics: "centroid_x": Longitude windshed "centroid". centroid mean lon-lat coordinates, weighed wind accessibility values x. "centroid_y": Latitude windshed centroid. "centroid_distance": Distance origin windshed centroid, km. "centroid_bearing": Bearing origin windshed centroid, degrees. "windshed_distance: Mean distance origin, km. average distance origin every grid cell, weighted accessibility. "windshed_bearing": Mean bearing origin, degrees. circular-mean bearing origin every grid cell, weighted accessibility. "windshed_isotropy": Circular standard deviation bearing origin every grid cell, weighted accessibility. Low values indicate accessible sites concentrated narrow range compass directions, high values indicate wide distribution directions. range possible values 0-1. "windshed_size": Mean accessibility. average accessibility values, weighted correct grid distortions. Higher values indicate landscapes greater overall wind accessibility. "windshed_landarea": realative measure land area covered grid cells nonzero wind accessibility.
